title: Batch Manufacturing Record Review
summary: Pre-review of executed batch manufacturing and packaging records that flags blank fields, out-of-limit values, signature gaps and unlinked deviations, with page references, before QA starts.

seo.title: AI Batch Manufacturing Record (BMR) Review | VipraTech
seo.description: AI pre-review of executed BMRs and BPRs that flags blank fields, out-of-limit values, missing signatures and open deviations for QA reviewers.

problem.intro: Executed batch manufacturing records (BMRs) and batch packaging records (BPRs) are still hand-filled on many sites, with in-process checks, equipment logs, line clearance and printouts attached. QA reads every page before release, and the record is often the slowest step between packing and dispatch.

pain_points.title: Every page read, every time
pain_points.detail: Reviewers check dispensing weights, process parameters, yield calculations and signatures page by page, even when most of the record is in order.

pain_points.title: Small errors found late
pain_points.detail: A missing second-person verification, an unrecorded time or a wrong yield calculation often surfaces at release and sends the record back to the floor.

pain_points.title: Deviations not linked
pain_points.detail: A parameter excursion noted in the margin may have no deviation number, or the deviation may still be open when the batch is presented for release.

pain_points.title: Good documentation practice slips
pain_points.detail: Overwriting, corrections without date and initials, and blank fields left unstruck are common audit observations that are tedious to catch by hand.

solution.overview: We build a review assistant that reads scanned or electronic batch records against the master record for that product. It extracts every entry, checks recorded values against the limits in the master BMR, recalculates yields and reconciliations, and confirms each step carries the required signatures and dates. It looks for good documentation practice issues such as blank fields and corrections without initials, and checks deviation and change control numbers against your QMS. The output is a findings sheet with each item linked to the page image, so QA reviews by exception and still signs off the whole record.
capabilities: Maps each executed page to its step in the master BMR or BPR
Reads handwritten entries, stamps and attached printouts such as weighing slips and HMI reports
Checks recorded parameters against master record limits and recalculates yield and reconciliation
Detects missing signatures, dates, second-person checks and unstruck blank fields
Matches deviation, OOS and change control references against the QMS and flags open items
Produces a findings sheet linked to page images for QA review and sign-off

workflow.title: Scan or export the executed record
workflow.detail: The completed BMR or BPR is scanned on the shop floor or exported from the MES and tagged with product and batch number.

workflow.title: Align to the master record
workflow.detail: Each page is matched to its master BMR step, so the expected fields, limits and signatories are known.

workflow.title: Extract entries
workflow.detail: Handwritten and printed values, signatures, dates and attachments are extracted with a confidence score per field.

workflow.title: Confirm unclear reads
workflow.detail: Fields the system cannot read confidently are shown to a reviewer to confirm instead of being guessed.

workflow.title: Run checks
workflow.detail: Values are compared with limits, calculations are repeated, GDP rules are applied and deviation references are matched to the QMS.

workflow.title: QA reviews findings
workflow.detail: The QA reviewer works through the findings sheet, returns corrections to production and completes the formal review.

inputs: Executed BMR and BPR scans or eBMR exports
Approved master BMR and BPR for the product
Attached printouts such as weighing slips, HMI reports and line clearance checklists
Deviation, OOS and change control register from the QMS
outputs: Findings sheet grouped by severity with page references
List of open or unlinked deviations
Extracted batch data for trending in your annual product quality review
Audit log of all checks and reviewer decisions
human_in_the_loop: Reviewers confirm any entry the system could not read confidently, and QA decides whether each finding is a genuine issue. Batch disposition stays with the Qualified Person or authorised QA; the assistant only prepares the review.
integrations: MES or eBMR system (export or API)
QMS such as TrackWise, MasterControl or an in-house system
Document management system holding master records
ERP batch status in SAP or similar
guardrails: No automatic batch disposition; release stays with authorised QA
Per-field confidence threshold, with unclear handwriting sent for confirmation
Check rules derived from the approved master record and version-controlled
Every finding linked to the source page image
Periodic full manual review of sampled batches to measure what the system missed
compliance_notes: Treated as a computerised system supporting GMP review and validated for that intended use, with audit trails aligned to 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11.
Supports good documentation practice and ALCOA+ data integrity expectations, including under India's revised Schedule M.

pilot.scope: One product and one record type, such as the granulation-to-compression BMR, using previously reviewed batches plus live batches in parallel.
deliverables: Check list derived from the master BMR and agreed with QA
Working pre-review pipeline on historical and live batches
Comparison report against findings from your manual review

what_we_measure.how: Findings from your completed manual reviews compared with what the assistant flagged on the same batches.
Findings the QA reviewer marks as not an issue, counted per batch.
Sampled extracted entries compared with the page image by a reviewer.
Timed QA review of comparable batches with and without the findings sheet.

faqs.q: Our BMRs are handwritten. Will this work?
faqs.a: Yes, that is the usual case. Extraction handles handwritten entries and stamps, and anything below the confidence threshold is shown to a reviewer rather than guessed. The pilot reports read accuracy separately for handwritten and printed fields.
No. It moves QA from reading every page to working through a findings sheet, but QA still reviews and signs the record. We also recommend periodic full manual review of sampled batches as a control.

faqs.q: We already run an eBMR. Is this still useful?
faqs.a: An eBMR enforces many entry checks at the point of entry. The assistant then focuses on cross-record checks: deviations, attachments, calculations and consistency with the QMS and LIMS.

faqs.q: How long does it take to add a new product?
faqs.a: Each product needs its master record mapped into checks. The pilot shows how long that takes for your record format, and later products reuse the same rule types.
